AI Broke Vulnerability Management. That's Why CISOs Are Moving Budget to BAS.

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 10 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

For thirty years, vulnerability management ran on a buffer: the months between when a vulnerability was found and when someone could figure out how to weaponize it. The solution was straightforward enough; triage by severity, schedule the fix, validate, and move on. The buffer was what made that work. Today, that buffer is gone. AI didn't make your team slower. It changed the other side of the

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin password spray at machine cadence (Feb 2026 MCP campaign) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] First-seen successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN auth from hosting ASN following failures · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Network appliance / jump host originating outbound HTTPS to LLM-API or MCP endpoints · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Sub-second cadence burst of FortiGate post-auth CLI/API commands (MCP autonomous execution) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin password spray at machine cadence (Feb 2026 MCP campaign) AIDelivery High
Hunts the credential-spray phase of the February 2026 MCP-orchestrated campaign against internet-exposed FortiGate appliances. Surfaces one source IP/ASN producing dozens of authentication failures across many distinct usernames or appliances inside a 10-minute window — the volumetric fingerprint of an LLM-driven offensive tool sweeping the actor's queue of 2,516 devices in 106 countries. Rationale: Article cites AWS-confirmed compromise of 600+ FortiGate devices across 55+ countries and actor logs queuing 2,516 in 106 countries, all driven by an MCP server running offensive tooling autonomously — the only practical detection on the credential-access phase is high-volume failed FortiGate auth from one source spanning many users/appliances. FortiGate logs surface via Sentinel CommonSecurityLog using DeviceVendor=Fortinet and DeviceExternalID for the appliance identifier. Cross-checked against: • https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/
ATT&CKT1110.001 T1110.003 T1133
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor-managed FortiGate fleet monitoring tool repeatedly logging in to many appliances from one source
  • Internal MSP/NOC IP running a credential-validity sweep after a password rotation
  • Authorised red-team / BAS engagement targeting the SSL-VPN portal
  • Misconfigured load-balancer NAT collapsing many user sessions behind one source IP
  • Mobile clients retrying with cached bad credentials after a policy change
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<msp-noc-cidr>","<bas-platform-cidr>"]))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the source IP's ASN, geo, and reputation; pivot to the appliance list and check whether any DestinationUserName saw a Success event in the same window from the same source IP. Step 2 (contain): block the source IP/ASN at the FortiGate WAN policy and force a credential rotation on any account that authenticated successfully from that IP in the prior 24h; revoke active SSL-VPN sessions. Step 3 (hunt): query CommonSecurityLog for the same SourceIP across other edge brands (Citrix, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA) — the MCP toolchain pivots opportunistically; check egress from the SOC's own FortiGate appliances for outbound HTTPS to LLM/MCP endpoints (the C2 UC).
let WindowMin = 10m;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 541)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionFailed")
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctTargets = dcount(RemoteIP),
            Targets = make_set(RemoteIP, 50)
            by InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where ConnCount > 200 and DistinctTargets > 20
// FortiGate SSL-VPN portal lives on 443/10443 — bursty fan-out to many external FGT hosts
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 10m;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("FortiGate","Fortigate","FortiOS")
| where (Activity has_any ("login failed","ssl-vpn login fail","admin login failed","authentication failed")
        or EventOutcome =~ "Failure"
        or DeviceAction =~ "deny")
| summarize FailCount = count(),
            DistinctUsers = dcount(DestinationHostName),
            DistinctAppliances = dcount(DeviceExternalID),
            Appliances = make_set(DeviceExternalID, 20),
            Users = make_set(DestinationHostName, 20)
            by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where FailCount > 50 and (DistinctUsers > 10 or DistinctAppliances > 5)   // 50 fails/10m = beyond typo cadence; spray fingerprint
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(fortinet OR fortigate OR syslog) (@Activity:*login*fail* OR @EventOutcome:Failure OR @evt.outcome:failure) @DeviceVendor:Fortinet
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Authentication.user) as DistinctUsers, dc(Authentication.dest) as DistinctAppliances, values(Authentication.dest) as Appliances, values(Authentication.user) as Users from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | where count > 50 AND (DistinctUsers > 10 OR DistinctAppliances > 5) | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Authentication.user) as DistinctUsers, dc(Authentication.dest) as DistinctAppliances, values(Authentication.dest) as Appliances, values(Authentication.user) as Users from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | where count > 50 AND (DistinctUsers > 10 OR DistinctAppliances > 5) | sort - _time
First-seen successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN auth from hosting ASN following failures AIExploitation High
Catches the initial-access pivot when the MCP-driven spray finally guesses a weak FortiGate admin or SSL-VPN credential. Joins a recent burst of failures from a source IP to a Success event for the same source/appliance pair — the exact shape AWS describes for the 600+ compromised devices, where no zero-day was used and the foothold came purely from weak creds on the public management/VPN surface. Rationale: Article: "AWS confirmed 600+ devices across 55+ countries" with "no zero-days needed, just weak credentials". The high-fidelity signal is the success-after-failure pattern from a single source against the same appliance — joins the credential_access spray to the initial_access foothold. CommonSecurityLog's DeviceExternalID is the FortiGate appliance identifier in CEF (DeviceName does not exist on this table). Cross-checked against: • https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/
ATT&CKT1078 T1133 T1110.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin who fat-fingered a password 20+ times then succeeded from the same office IP
  • Helpdesk reset workflow where a tech repeatedly tested an account before handing off to the user
  • Authorised red-team / BAS engagement validating SSL-VPN auth
  • Roaming user behind a CGNAT whose source IP also serves a brute-force tool on another tenant
  • MFA failure logs landing in the wrong bucket and being counted as auth failures
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<corp-egress-cidr>","<msp-noc-cidr>","<bas-platform-cidr>"]))
| where DestinationUserName !in~ ("<bas-test-account>","<redteam-account>")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): enrich SourceIP with ASN / hosting-provider data; an ASN belonging to a VPS/hosting provider (DigitalOcean, OVH, Hetzner, Choopa, M247) following a spray is treated as confirmed initial access until proven otherwise. Step 2 (contain): immediately disable the compromised account, revoke its active VPN sessions, block the source IP at the WAN edge, and snapshot the appliance config for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): inside the appliance, list config changes (especially admin user adds, local-in policy edits, port forwards, new VIPs) and SSL-VPN tunnel mode sessions in the 24h after the success; pivot to the C2 UC to look for outbound HTTPS from the appliance to LLM-API or unknown JSON-RPC endpoints.
// Defender XDR does not see FortiGate auth — endpoint-side proxy for this UC is a successful inbound RDP/SMB from the same external IP shortly after a spray, but the canonical detection lives in Sentinel CommonSecurityLog. Use the sentinel_kql query.
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("Network","RemoteInteractive")
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP) and RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP, LogonType
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 7d;
let Failures = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
    | where DeviceProduct has_any ("FortiGate","Fortigate","FortiOS")
    | where Activity has_any ("login failed","ssl-vpn login fail","admin login failed","authentication failed")
         or EventOutcome =~ "Failure"
    | summarize FailCount = count(), FirstFail = min(TimeGenerated), LastFail = max(TimeGenerated)
                by SourceIP, DeviceExternalID, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
    | where FailCount >= 20;     // 20 in 30m = sustained spray, not a typo
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("FortiGate","Fortigate","FortiOS")
| where Activity has_any ("login","ssl-vpn login","admin login","authentication success")
     and EventOutcome =~ "Success"
| join kind=inner Failures on SourceIP, DeviceExternalID
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, LastFail)
| where DelayMin between (0 .. 60)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, ApplianceID = DeviceExternalID, DestinationHostName, FailCount, FirstFail, LastFail, DelayMin
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(fortinet OR fortigate OR syslog) @DeviceVendor:Fortinet (@Activity:*login* OR @evt.name:*login*) (@EventOutcome:Success OR @evt.outcome:success)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count as Successes, values(Authentication.user) as Users, values(Authentication.dest) as Appliances from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | join type=inner Authentication.src [ | tstats `summariesonly` count as Failures from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | where Failures >= 20 ] | where Successes >= 1 | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count as Successes, values(Authentication.user) as Users, values(Authentication.dest) as Appliances from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | join type=inner Authentication.src [ | tstats summariesonly=false count as Failures from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.app IN ("fortigate","fortios","ssl-vpn","fortigate-admin") by Authentication.src, _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name("Authentication")` | where Failures >= 20 ] | where Successes >= 1 | sort - _time
Sub-second cadence burst of FortiGate post-auth CLI/API commands (MCP autonomous execution) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the execution phase of the MCP campaign on a freshly-compromised FortiGate: an authenticated session issues a burst of CLI/API commands at sub-second cadence — a rate no human admin can produce. The article's distinguishing feature vs traditional FortiGate compromise is that the post-auth tooling ran autonomously through an MCP server, not a human at a terminal, so the temporal fingerprint becomes the detection. Rationale: Article: "a custom MCP server running offensive tools autonomously" — the autonomous brain is what differentiates this campaign from a hands-on-keyboard FortiGate compromise. The temporal fingerprint (sub-second cadence of CLI/config-change events under one session) is the cleanest article-specific pivot. Uses CommonSecurityLog with DeviceExternalID for appliance identification (the previous DeviceName usage was schema-invalid). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
ATT&CKT1059 T1106 T1078
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated FortiGate config backup / compliance tool (FortiManager, Tufin, AlgoSec) running a scheduled pull
  • Zero-touch provisioning script applying a baseline to a newly-onboarded appliance
  • FortiManager pushing a policy package across many appliances simultaneously
  • FortiAnalyzer or NOC dashboard polling 'diagnose' / 'get system' status at high frequency
  • Authorised BAS / red-team automation exercising the management plane
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<fortimanager-ip>","<fortianalyzer-ip>","<noc-poller-cidr>"]))
| where SourceUserName !in~ ("fortimanager","backup-svc","compliance-svc")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the SourceUserName and SourceIP — is it a known FortiManager/orchestration system, or a SSL-VPN/admin login that should never drive config changes? Cross-reference with the initial-access UC: if this user authenticated 0–60 minutes earlier from a hosting ASN after a spray, escalate immediately. Step 2 (contain): kill the active admin/CLI session, force-disable the user, snapshot the running and startup configs and diff against the last known-good. Step 3 (hunt): walk the SampleCmds set for added admins, new local-in policies, SSL-VPN portal edits, or new port-forwards/VIPs; pivot to the C2 UC for outbound HTTPS from the appliance and to any newly-created admin accounts being reused on other appliances in the fleet.
// FortiGate CLI/API audit does not ship to Defender XDR — canonical detection is in Sentinel via CommonSecurityLog. Endpoint-side proxy: a single user's account driving sub-second remote operations against many internal hosts can be approximated via DeviceLogonEvents fan-out.
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where LogonType in ("Network","RemoteInteractive")
| summarize Logons = count(), Targets = dcount(DeviceId)
            by AccountName, RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where Logons > 30 and Targets > 10
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("FortiGate","Fortigate","FortiOS")
| where Activity has_any ("execute","config","diagnose","get system","cli","api call","edit","set","unset")
     or DeviceEventClassID has_any ("cfg-","cli-","event-system")
| summarize CmdCount = count(),
            DistinctCmds = dcount(Activity),
            SampleCmds = make_set(Activity, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by ApplianceID = DeviceExternalID, SourceUserName, SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 10s)
| where CmdCount > 20                                  // 20 distinct CLI/config ops in 10s
| extend RateCmdsPerSec = todouble(CmdCount) / 10.0
| where RateCmdsPerSec > 2                             // > 2 ops/sec is super-human cadence
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(fortinet OR fortigate OR syslog) @DeviceVendor:Fortinet (@Activity:(execute OR config OR diagnose OR "get system" OR edit OR set))
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count as CmdCount, values(All_Changes.command) as Commands, min(_time) as FirstSeen, max(_time) as LastSeen from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.vendor_product IN ("FortiGate","FortiOS") All_Changes.action IN ("executed","modified","created","deleted") by All_Changes.user, All_Changes.src, All_Changes.dest, _time span=10s | `drop_dm_object_name("All_Changes")` | where CmdCount > 20 | eval RateCmdsPerSec = CmdCount / 10.0 | where RateCmdsPerSec > 2 | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count as CmdCount, values(All_Changes.command) as Commands, min(_time) as FirstSeen, max(_time) as LastSeen from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.vendor_product IN ("FortiGate","FortiOS") All_Changes.action IN ("executed","modified","created","deleted") by All_Changes.user, All_Changes.src, All_Changes.dest, _time span=10s | `drop_dm_object_name("All_Changes")` | where CmdCount > 20 | eval RateCmdsPerSec = CmdCount / 10.0 | where RateCmdsPerSec > 2 | sort - _time
Network appliance / jump host originating outbound HTTPS to LLM-API or MCP endpoints AICommand & Control Medium
Catches the C2 channel of the autonomous MCP campaign: edge appliances and jump hosts should never originate outbound traffic to Anthropic / OpenAI / Bedrock or to unknown JSON-RPC endpoints, but the article describes a custom MCP server brokering tasks between the LLM and the compromised fleet. Surfaces first-seen outbound to LLM-API FQDNs from devices in the network-infrastructure tier. Rationale: Kill-chain reconstruction explicitly calls out "Outbound HTTPS/JSON-RPC from network appliances or jump hosts to LLM-API or MCP-style endpoints" as the C2 fingerprint for this campaign, and the article frames the MCP server as the "orchestration brain" between the LLM and the compromised fleet. Edge devices originating AI-API traffic is a near-zero-baseline behaviour, so first-seen alone is high-signal. Cross-checked against: • https://modelcontextprotocol.io/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised AI-assistant pilot deployed onto a bastion / jump host for ops automation
  • Vendor support tool on a network appliance that legitimately calls an LLM (e.g. Fortinet FortiAI, Palo Alto Precision AI)
  • Misclassified asset tag — a developer workstation incorrectly tagged as 'jumphost' calling api.openai.com for normal IDE use
  • Outbound proxy is a CDN-edge IP that also fronts the LLM endpoint, producing false-positive SNI matches
  • Security tool (BAS, scanner) running its own LLM-assisted analysis from a tagged DMZ host
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ (dynamic(["<approved-ai-pilot-host>","<bas-platform-host>"]))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the source asset and confirm its role — is it a FortiGate, F5, jump host, or actually a misclassified user box? Pull the full DNS / SNI history for the asset in the last 7d and any auth events from the appliance UI immediately before the outbound. Step 2 (contain): if the asset is an edge appliance or bastion, block egress to the LLM FQDNs at the proxy/firewall and snapshot the device for forensics; do not reboot — MCP/agent state may live only in memory. Step 3 (hunt): pivot to the FortiGate auth UCs to find the matching initial-access event for the appliance, then sweep the fleet for the same outbound destinations from other devices in the infra tier; check for newly-created admin accounts whose creation timestamp falls within the C2 window.
let LLMHosts = dynamic([
    "api.anthropic.com","claude.ai",
    "api.openai.com","chat.openai.com",
    "bedrock-runtime","generativelanguage.googleapis.com",
    "api.mistral.ai","api.deepseek.com","api.x.ai"
]);
DeviceInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceCategory in~ ("NetworkDevice","Server")
   or DeviceType in~ ("NetworkDevice","Firewall","Router")
   or RegistryDeviceTag has_any ("jumphost","bastion","edge","dmz")
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, DeviceCategory, RegistryDeviceTag
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
    | where RemotePort in (443, 8443)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (LLMHosts)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("mcp","model-context-protocol","jsonrpc")
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceCategory, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let LLMHosts = dynamic([
    "api.anthropic.com","claude.ai",
    "api.openai.com","chat.openai.com",
    "bedrock-runtime","generativelanguage.googleapis.com",
    "api.mistral.ai","api.deepseek.com","api.x.ai"
]);
let InfraSrcIPs = DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DeviceCategory in~ ("NetworkDevice","Server")
        or DeviceType in~ ("NetworkDevice","Firewall","Router")
        or RegistryDeviceTag has_any ("jumphost","bastion","edge","dmz")
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId
    | mv-expand PublicIP
    | project PublicIP = tostring(PublicIP);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceAction !~ "deny"
| where DestinationPort in (443, 8443)
| where (DestinationHostName has_any (LLMHosts) or RequestURL has_any (LLMHosts) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (LLMHosts))
| join kind=inner (InfraSrcIPs) on $left.SourceIP == $right.PublicIP
| project TimeGenerated, ApplianceID = DeviceExternalID, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Edge appliance or jump host outbound to LLM-API endpoint
id: 7b8c19a4-2f3e-4c5a-9b62-1d4e7f8a9b03
description: Detects an outbound HTTPS connection to a known LLM-API FQDN originating from a device tagged as edge infrastructure, jump host, or bastion. This is the C2 fingerprint of the Feb 2026 MCP-orchestrated FortiGate campaign — appliances should never originate AI-API traffic.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-broke-vulnerability-management-thats.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort:
      - 443
      - 8443
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - api.anthropic.com
      - claude.ai
      - api.openai.com
      - bedrock-runtime
      - generativelanguage.googleapis.com
      - api.mistral.ai
      - api.deepseek.com
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorised AI-integration pilots running on infra-tier hosts
  - Vendor support tooling that legitimately calls an LLM API from a bastion
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:fortinet OR source:paloalto OR source:zeek) @DestinationPort:(443 OR 8443) (@DestinationHostname:(api.anthropic.com OR claude.ai OR api.openai.com OR *bedrock-runtime* OR generativelanguage.googleapis.com OR api.mistral.ai OR api.deepseek.com) OR @network.destination.domain:(api.anthropic.com OR api.openai.com OR api.mistral.ai))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(api\.anthropic\.com|claude\.ai|api\.openai\.com|bedrock-runtime.*\.amazonaws\.com|generativelanguage\.googleapis\.com|api\.mistral\.ai|api\.deepseek\.com|api\.x\.ai)$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(sshd|openvpn|forticlient|ssl-vpn|putty|plink|jumphost|bastion|nginx|haproxy)/i OR regex("\\\\(System32|Program Files)\\\\(OpenSSH|Forti)", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Web.url) as URLs, values(Web.user) as Users, min(_time) as FirstSeen from datamodel=Web where Web.dest IN ("api.anthropic.com","api.openai.com","bedrock-runtime.*.amazonaws.com","generativelanguage.googleapis.com","api.mistral.ai","api.deepseek.com") by Web.src, Web.dest, host | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")` | lookup network_infra_assets src OUTPUT asset_tier | where asset_tier IN ("edge-appliance","jump-host","firewall","vpn-gateway") | sort - FirstSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.url) as URLs, values(Web.user) as Users, min(_time) as FirstSeen from datamodel=Web where Web.dest IN ("api.anthropic.com","api.openai.com","bedrock-runtime.*.amazonaws.com","generativelanguage.googleapis.com","api.mistral.ai","api.deepseek.com") by Web.src, Web.dest, host | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")` | lookup network_infra_assets src OUTPUT asset_tier | where asset_tier IN ("edge-appliance","jump-host","firewall","vpn-gateway") | sort - FirstSeen
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| sort - count

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FireAnt Metakit.exe spawns unsigned setup.exe update payload AIDelivery High
Detects the FireAnt Metakit supply chain abuse where Metakit.exe launches a tampered setup.exe pulled from metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml without integrity validation. This is the specific delivery pivot for the OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER campaign against Vietnamese stock investors. Rationale: Article names Metakit.exe specifically as the parent that executed the malicious setup.exe due to absent signature validation on metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml. The parent-child pair is unique to the FireAnt update flow and is the cleanest delivery pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate signed FireAnt platform updates where setup.exe is the genuine vendor binary
  • IT-staged Metakit deployment using a renamed installer named setup.exe
  • Endpoint penetration test mimicking the FireAnt update mechanism
  • Forensic replay of historical Metakit updates in lab/sandbox imagery
Suppression filter
and not (SHA256 in ("<known-good-FireAnt-setup-sha256>")) and not (InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "FireAnt" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "FireAnt")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull SHA1/SHA256 of the spawned setup.exe and check against the article's hashes (865A1739..., B0FEA981..., 48FEBB91..., 511B7745..., 8CD78B8D...) and VirusTotal. Confirm download source URL from web proxy / DeviceFileEvents FileOriginUrl. 2. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Machine Action, block the spawned hash org-wide, sinkhole metakit.fireant[.]vn at the proxy until FireAnt confirms a legitimate vendor update. 3. Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA1 of Metakit.exe across all investor-segment hosts, look for subsequent DLL side-loading (DtlCrashCatch.dll) and OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection, and any beacons to financemachinelearning[.]com.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe" or ProcessCommandLine has "setup.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Metakit.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\setup.exe" or CommandLine has "setup.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load via DtlCrashCatch.dll AIInstallation High
Hunts the specific side-loading DLL named in the ESET report — DtlCrashCatch.dll — being loaded by a legitimate signed Windows binary used as the loader. This is the immediate post-delivery stage in both the FireAnt and Transport-construction-firm clusters. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is the verbatim rogue DLL named in the ESET write-up. The filename is unique enough that any creation or load is essentially a confirmed SPECTRALVIPER stage. Cross-checked against MITRE ATT&CK G0050 side-loading TTPs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Dell DataSafe component named identically (verify by signing cert)
  • Security researcher lab replication of the OceanLotus chain
  • Incident-response replay of captured samples on a forensic workstation
  • Sandbox detonation of the captured IOC by SOC tooling
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the DLL, run sigcheck and compare SHA1 to the article's hashes; pull the parent loader process to confirm side-loading vs legitimate load. 2. Contain: isolate the device, block the DLL hash via Defender IOC, kill the loader process. 3. Hunt: enumerate all hosts that ever wrote DtlCrashCatch.dll across the last 90d, check for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection events and outbound connections to financemachinelearning[.]com or gatewayrvcenter[.]com.
union
( DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll" and ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe AIInstallation Medium
Detects the SPECTRALVIPER loader injecting into the legitimate Microsoft binary OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe — a hollowing/injection target unique to this campaign chain per ESET. Hunts unexpected parent-spawn patterns and out-of-folder OneDrive process behaviour. Rationale: ESET explicitly states the rogue DtlCrashCatch.dll injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to launch SPECTRALVIPER. Filtering for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe with unexpected parent or path catches the hollowing target without flagging legitimate OneDrive sync activity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/012/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom OneDrive deployments in non-standard install paths (per-app virtualisation)
  • OneDrive update in progress where path is briefly off the canonical folder
  • Microsoft Intune script-based OneDrive provisioning
  • User-installed OneDrive in %LocalAppData% (handled by the OR condition — review folder)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "Microsoft Corporation" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "Microsoft Corporation" and FolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft\OneDrive\", @"\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the loaded image list of the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process, look for DtlCrashCatch.dll and any unsigned modules. Pull SHA256 and check article hashes. 2. Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, block the loader hash, quarantine the dropped DLL. 3. Hunt: across estate, look for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe initiating outbound connections to financemachinelearning[.]com / gatewayrvcenter[.]com — a normal OneDrive process never talks to those.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft\OneDrive\", @"\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\"))
   or not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","services.exe","svchost.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where not (NewProcessName has_any (@"\Microsoft\OneDrive\", @"\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\"))
   or not (ParentProcessName endswith "\\OneDrive.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\services.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\svchost.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(OneDrive\.exe|OneDriveStandaloneUpdater\.exe|services\.exe|svchost\.exe)$/i AND ImageFileName=/\\(Microsoft\\OneDrive|Program Files\\Microsoft OneDrive)\\/i)

SPECTRALVIPER C2 domain or IP resolution/connection (FireAnt + MSSQL campaigns) AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on DNS or network egress to the named SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure (financemachinelearning[.]com, gatewayrvcenter[.]com, plus published IPs) from any host in the estate. High-fidelity IOC hits. Rationale: Domains and IPs are directly named in the article and in pre-extracted IOCs. financemachinelearning[.]com is the FireAnt cluster C2; gatewayrvcenter[.]com is the transport-construction cluster C2. Cross-checked against MITRE ATT&CK G0050. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform validating IOCs by sending test queries
  • Security researcher / sandbox detonating samples
  • DNS sinkhole rewrites where the resolver itself logs the queried name
  • Honeypot deliberately resolving the indicators for telemetry
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and AccountName has "researcher")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the initiating process; if non-OneDrive process is dialling out, treat as confirmed SPECTRALVIPER beacon. Pull host context (Vietnam investor or transport-construction segment). 2. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Machine Action, sinkhole all six C2 domains at the DNS resolver and block all eight IPs at the perimeter firewall. Block the initiating-process SHA256. 3. Hunt: search 90 days back across estate for any historical resolution of these domains, look for sibling indicators (Metakit.exe→setup.exe, DtlCrashCatch.dll, the article's SHA1 hashes).
let c2_domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2_ips)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2_domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has_any (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Query=Name, Dest=tostring(IPAddresses) ),
( CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2_domains) or DestinationIP in (c2_ips) or RequestURL has_any (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Dest=DestinationIP ),
( ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, Dest=DstIpAddr ),
( ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in (c2_ips) or DstHostname has_any (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=DstHostname, Dest=DstIpAddr )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER known-bad SHA1 execution / file write AIInstallation Medium
High-confidence IOC match for the five SHA1 hashes ESET published as SPECTRALVIPER components across the FireAnt and Transport Construction Corp clusters. Fires on any process execution, image load or file write matching these hashes. Rationale: Five SHA1 IOCs are listed in the pre-extracted IOCs from ESET reporting. Pure-IOC hits are the highest-fidelity detection possible — any match is confirmed SPECTRALVIPER. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1027 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / forensic analyst replaying samples in a controlled lab
  • EDR vendor's threat-intel collection process
  • Security researcher's static analysis sandbox
  • Hash collisions are vanishingly rare for SHA1 in this context — effectively zero
Response runbook
1. Triage: immediately treat any hit as confirmed SPECTRALVIPER — no further triage required for the IOC match itself, but pull host telemetry to scope blast radius. 2. Contain: isolate host, block hashes via Defender custom IOC + AV, kill the process, preserve disk image. 3. Hunt: pivot on DeviceId to retrieve all process executions, network connections, file writes in the 30 days before/after; cross-reference against the other UCs (C2 domains, DtlCrashCatch.dll, OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection).
let spectralviper_sha1 = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(60d) | where SHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) | project Timestamp, Source="Process", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(60d) | where SHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) | project Timestamp, Source="FileWrite", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(60d) | where SHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) | project Timestamp, Source="ImageLoad", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc

( ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d) | where SHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA1 ),
( ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d) | where TargetFileSHA1 in (spectralviper_sha1) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName=ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA1=TargetFileSHA1 ),

| order by TimeGenerated desc

OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe beaconing to non-Microsoft destination AICommand & Control Medium
Behavioural detection: the legitimate OneDrive Sync client should only talk to Microsoft IP ranges. SPECTRALVIPER injects into it and beacons to attacker C2 — so OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe contacting any non-Microsoft endpoint is high-signal regardless of whether the C2 domain is already known. Rationale: Article states SPECTRALVIPER is launched inside OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe via injection from DtlCrashCatch.dll. Genuine OneDrive sync traffic stays inside Microsoft's ASN — any non-Microsoft public destination from this process is anomalous and matches the campaign behaviour without depending on the specific C2 domains being known. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/required-urls-and-ports • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1055.012
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Telemetry / diagnostics endpoints not on Microsoft domains (rare, narrow set)
  • Corporate proxy substitution where the resolved IP is the proxy rather than the Microsoft service
  • Third-party CDN occasionally used by OneDrive (verify the IP against Microsoft published ranges)
  • Network test connectivity probes (msftconnecttest is allow-listed)
Suppression filter
and not (RemoteUrl has_any ("akadns.net","akamaiedge.net","trafficmanager.net") and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "Microsoft Corporation")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the destination is not in Microsoft's published service IPs/URLs (https://learn.microsoft.com/...). Pull loaded modules of the offending OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process — look for DtlCrashCatch.dll or any unsigned DLL. 2. Contain: isolate host, block the remote IP/domain at the perimeter, kill the OneDrive process. 3. Hunt: cross-correlate with C2 IOC hits, SHA1 IOC hits, and Metakit.exe→setup.exe events on the same host or estate.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("microsoft.com","onedrive.com","sharepoint.com","office.com","live.com","azureedge.net","windows.net","officeapps.live.com","msocdn.com","msftconnecttest.com"))
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), AnyCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), AnyFolder = any(InitiatingProcessFolderPath) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" or ActingProcessName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| where not (DstHostname has_any ("microsoft.com","onedrive.com","sharepoint.com","office.com","live.com","azureedge.net","windows.net","officeapps.live.com","msocdn.com","msftconnecttest.com"))
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe OR *\onedrive.sync.service.exe) NOT @DestinationHostname:(*.microsoft.com OR *.onedrive.com OR *.sharepoint.com OR *.office.com OR *.live.com OR *.azureedge.net OR *.windows.net OR *.officeapps.live.com OR *.msocdn.com)
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest) ContextImageFileName=/\\OneDrive\.Sync\.Service\.exe$/i
| NOT (DomainName=/(microsoft|onedrive|sharepoint|office|live|azureedge|windows|officeapps|msocdn|msftconnecttest)\.(com|net)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" AND NOT All_Traffic.dest IN ("*.microsoft.com","*.onedrive.com","*.sharepoint.com","*.office.com","*.live.com","*.azureedge.net","*.windows.net","*.officeapps.live.com","*.msocdn.com","*.msftconnecttest.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" AND NOT All_Traffic.dest IN ("*.microsoft.com","*.onedrive.com","*.sharepoint.com","*.office.com","*.live.com","*.azureedge.net","*.windows.net","*.officeapps.live.com","*.msocdn.com","*.msftconnecttest.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
MSSQL service spawning interactive shell or LOLBin (initial access into Transport Construction Corp cluster) AIExploitation High
Hunts the suspected initial access vector for the second OceanLotus cluster — exploitation of a public-facing Microsoft SQL Server leading to sqlservr.exe spawning interactive shells or LOLBins. Targets the post-exploitation T-SQL→OS-command pivot. Rationale: Article explicitly notes 'exploitation of remote code execution vulnerabilities in a public-facing Microsoft SQL server' as the suspected initial access for the transport-construction-firm cluster. xp_cmdshell-style abuse produces sqlservr.exe→cmd.exe child chains. Pairs cleanly with the rest of the SPECTRALVIPER detections to scope the second cluster. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1505.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DBA running maintenance jobs via xp_cmdshell legitimately
  • Backup/monitoring scripts invoked by SQL Server Agent
  • Third-party SQL extension that legitimately shells out (e.g. PolyBase, R Services)
  • SCCM/Intune client management running under SQL service account context
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("<dba-svc-account>","sqlagent") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("backup","maintenance","sp_executesql"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture full ProcessCommandLine and check for reconnaissance (whoami, net user, systeminfo) or download primitives (certutil -urlcache, curl). Identify whether the MSSQL instance is internet-facing. 2. Contain: isolate the SQL host, disable xp_cmdshell via sp_configure, rotate the SQL service account, block any C2 destinations contacted from the host. 3. Hunt: pull the SQL Server error log and any audit trail for the originating client IP, search the estate for the same source IP across other public-facing services, look for SPECTRALVIPER hash/domain IOCs on the host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sqlservr.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","mshta.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\sqlservr.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\wmic.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\systeminfo.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MSSQL sqlservr.exe Spawning Shell or LOLBin (OceanLotus MSSQL Initial Access)
id: 9a4c1e23-2f7b-4f81-bc8d-0e9d12c4f2a1
description: Detects sqlservr.exe spawning command shells or LOLBins — likely xp_cmdshell or stored-procedure abuse used by OceanLotus to gain initial access into a Vietnamese transport construction firm via a public-facing MSSQL server.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1505.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\sqlservr.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\systeminfo.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\sqlservr.exe OR *\SQLSERVR.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\net.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^sqlservr\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|mshta|regsvr32|rundll32|wmic|wscript|cscript|net|net1|whoami|systeminfo)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="sqlservr.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","mshta.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="sqlservr.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","mshta.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
FireAnt Metakit downloader HTTP POST to staging server with host recon AIDelivery Medium
Detects the FireAnt-delivered downloader stage that performs basic host reconnaissance and POSTs the data to a staging server before pulling next-stage SPECTRALVIPER. Pivots on Metakit-spawned binaries making outbound HTTP POSTs to non-FireAnt destinations. Rationale: ESET notes the downloader 'performed basic host reconnaissance and transmitted the collected information via an HTTP POST request to a staging server, requesting the next-stage payload.' Pinning to Metakit→setup.exe parent chain + non-FireAnt egress within 10m is the tightest signature available. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1082/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1082
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt setup.exe contacting telemetry endpoints not under the fireant.vn apex
  • Endpoint AV/EDR sandboxing the setup.exe in a controlled detonation
  • FireAnt-bundled third-party SDKs that beacon to vendor analytics
  • Outdated FireAnt installer reaching legacy update CDN
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the destination's WHOIS/ASN; check whether it matches OceanLotus C2 ASN history. Capture setup.exe SHA256 and submit to VT/Hybrid Analysis. 2. Contain: isolate the host, block destination at perimeter and DNS, quarantine setup.exe. 3. Hunt: pivot on the staging destination across the estate, look for other Metakit-driven downloads, retrospectively review all FireAnt update activity since 2025-10-02.
let MetakitChildren = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
    | project DeviceId, ChildPid = ProcessId, ChildName = FileName, ChildStart = Timestamp;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not (RemoteUrl endswith "fireant.vn")
| join kind=inner MetakitChildren on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ChildPid
| where Timestamp between (ChildStart .. ChildStart + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let metakitChildren = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Metakit.exe"
    | project Computer, ChildPid = NewProcessId, ChildName = NewProcessName, ChildStart = TimeGenerated;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| where not (DstHostname endswith "fireant.vn")
| join kind=inner (metakitChildren) on $left.SrcHostname == $right.Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (ChildStart .. ChildStart + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, ActingProcessName, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @ParentImage:(*\Metakit.exe OR *\metakit.exe) NOT @DestinationHostname:*.fireant.vn
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^metakit\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i | groupBy(aid, function=min(_time, as=childStart))}, field=aid)
| _time>=childStart AND _time<=childStart+600
| NOT DomainName=/fireant\.vn$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(All_Traffic.dest) as destinations min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.process_name="setup.exe" OR All_Traffic.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe") AND NOT All_Traffic.dest IN ("metakit.fireant.vn","fireant.vn","*.fireant.vn") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Traffic.dest) as destinations min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.process_name="setup.exe" OR All_Traffic.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe") AND NOT All_Traffic.dest IN ("metakit.fireant.vn","fireant.vn","*.fireant.vn") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

ATT&CKT1071

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
