Dependency Confusion or Typosquatting Installation AIDelivery Low
Hunts for npm install commands pulling packages from non-default registries or packages whose names closely resemble known organisational/internal prefixes — the dependency-confusion path that GitHub's --allow-remote default closure is partly aimed at. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit mention of --allow-git and --allow-remote becoming non-default in npm 12, plus git+/tarball dependency resolution paths. Excludes default registries to suppress baseline npm usage. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal artifact registries (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio) configured via --registry
  • Forked GitHub repos pulled as direct git dependencies in monorepos
  • Yarn workspaces that legitimately resolve git+ssh dependencies
  • Local development against feature branches via `npm install github:org/repo#branch`
  • Lockfile-driven CI installs after intentional upgrade to a pre-release published as a tarball URL
Suppression filter
and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("artifactory","nexus","verdaccio","jfrog","<your-internal-registry-hostname>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full command line and identify the package + registry/URL being installed. Cross-reference against the org's approved internal-registry list and the repo's package.json/package-lock.json. 2) Contain — if the registry/URL is unsanctioned, block at proxy/firewall, remove the package from the host, and rotate any npm tokens stored on that host. 3) Hunt — search lockfiles across all repos for the same registry/URL pattern, query DNS logs for the unsanctioned host, and inspect any CI pipelines using --allow-remote or --allow-git for unapproved sources.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--registry","--allow-remote","--allow-git","git+ssh://","git+https://","github:","gitlab:","bitbucket:")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"https?://[^/\s]+\.tgz"
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","npm.pkg.github.com"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "yarn.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "pnpm.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--registry","--allow-remote","--allow-git","git+ssh://","git+https://","github:","gitlab:","bitbucket:")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"https?://[^/\s]+\.tgz"
| where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","npm.pkg.github.com"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm Install with Non-Default Registry or Remote URL Dependency
id: 9b2c5d8e-3f4a-4b6c-8d1e-2a3b4c5d6e7f
description: Detects npm/node/yarn/pnpm invocations using --registry, --allow-remote, --allow-git, or direct git+/tarball URLs — paths GitHub is closing by default in npm 12.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  npm_cli:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  suspicious_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--registry'
      - '--allow-remote'
      - '--allow-git'
      - 'git+ssh://'
      - 'git+https://'
      - 'github:'
      - 'gitlab:'
  default_registry:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'registry.npmjs.org'
      - 'registry.yarnpkg.com'
      - 'npm.pkg.github.com'
  condition: npm_cli and suspicious_args and not default_registry
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\NPM.exe) (@CommandLine:(*--registry* OR *--allow-remote* OR *--allow-git* OR *git+ssh* OR *git+https* OR *github:* OR *gitlab:*)) -@CommandLine:(*registry.npmjs.org* OR *registry.yarnpkg.com* OR *npm.pkg.github.com*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| regex("(--registry|--allow-remote|--allow-git|git\+ssh://|git\+https://|github:|gitlab:)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT regex("(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|npm\.pkg\.github\.com)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") (Processes.process="*--registry*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*git+*" OR Processes.process="*github:*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-remote*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-git*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") (Processes.process="*--registry*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*git+*" OR Processes.process="*github:*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-remote*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-git*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Suspicious npm Registry Authentication or Publish Activity AIInstallation Medium
Detects npm login/publish operations and .npmrc modifications that introduce or alter auth tokens — a signal of package-hijack staging or token theft in advance of malicious package republication. Rationale: Targets npm-CLI operations explicitly tied to registry auth/publish workflow (npm publish, npm login, token create) plus .npmrc file writes — the staging surface for the package-hijack scenario the article alludes to. Two correlated tables make the signal pivot-able. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-publish • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Maintainer workstations doing legitimate `npm publish` to internal registry
  • CI/CD runners publishing packages on tag-push (these should be allowlisted by host)
  • Developers running `npm login` once per quarter when tokens rotate
  • yarn/pnpm wrapper tools that write to .npmrc on `yarn config set` calls
  • npm version bump scripts that touch .npmrc to set always-auth=true
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName in ("<known-ci-runner-1>","<known-ci-runner-2>") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runner.exe","agent.exe","jenkins.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify which package was being published, which auth token was used (~/.npmrc), and whether the host is an authorised maintainer/CI runner. Diff the published version against the source repo HEAD to spot timing gaps. 2) Contain — if unauthorised: revoke the npm token immediately (npm token revoke), unpublish/deprecate the suspect version, force-rotate any tokens in the .npmrc file. Block the host from the npm registry at the proxy. 3) Hunt — search for prior publishes from the same token, look at the host's process tree for token exfiltration (curl/wget reading .npmrc), and audit all packages owned by the affected maintainer account.
let PublishEvents = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish","npm login","npm adduser","npm token create","npm token revoke","--otp");
let NpmrcWrites = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName == ".npmrc"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$";
union PublishEvents, NpmrcWrites
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=coalesce(AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName), FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let PublishEvents = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish","npm login","npm adduser","npm token create","npm token revoke","--otp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType="PublishOrLogin";
let NpmrcWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType="NpmrcWrite";
union PublishEvents, NpmrcWrites
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:1 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPM.exe) @CommandLine:(*"npm publish"* OR *"npm login"* OR *"npm adduser"* OR *"npm token create"* OR *"npm token revoke"* OR *--otp*)) OR (@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.npmrc OR *\\.NPMRC)))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx)\.exe$/i regex("(npm publish|npm login|npm adduser|npm token (create|revoke)|--otp)", field=CommandLine)) OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\\.npmrc$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*npm login*" OR Processes.process="*npm token*" OR Processes.process="*npm adduser*" OR Processes.process="*--otp*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*npm login*" OR Processes.process="*npm token*" OR Processes.process="*npm adduser*" OR Processes.process="*--otp*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Lateral Movement via Compromised Transitive Dependency AIInstallation Low
Hunts for execution of binaries dropped under node_modules/.bin/ or transitive node_modules paths spawning from unusual parents — the blast-radius path of a transitive-dependency compromise that npm 12's allowScripts default is intended to neutralise. Rationale: Pivot anchored on the node_modules path the article identifies as the transitive-execution surface (any dep can run code via install hooks). LOLBin + path filter is what differentiates ransomware/loader traffic from legit Node tooling.
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • esbuild/webpack/tsc/eslint binaries shelling out to cmd.exe to invoke platform helpers
  • node-gyp builds invoking cmd.exe → cl.exe under node_modules\node-gyp\
  • Cypress / Playwright launching browsers that spawn helper processes
  • Husky git hooks running bash.exe from node_modules\husky\
  • ESM resolver shims invoking node.exe from node_modules\.bin\
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\esbuild\\","\\node_modules\\webpack\\","\\node_modules\\.bin\\tsc","\\node_modules\\.bin\\eslint","\\node_modules\\husky\\","\\node_modules\\cypress\\","\\node_modules\\playwright\\","\\node_modules\\node-gyp\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify the exact package (path under node_modules/<pkg>/) the binary executed from. Map to package.json + lockfile entry, capture version + integrity hash. Check npm advisory DB and ThreatFox for the package@version. 2) Contain — kill the process, isolate the host, remove node_modules and the lockfile entry, rotate any credentials/tokens the package might have read (env vars, .npmrc, ~/.aws/, ~/.ssh/). 3) Hunt — search all repos for the package@version in lockfiles, identify any CI/CD runner that installed it, and audit network egress from those hosts during the install window for C2 traffic.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has "\\node_modules\\"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\node_modules\\"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\.bin\\","\\node_modules\\")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand")
   or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\node_modules\\" and FileName !in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","esbuild.exe","webpack.exe","tsc.exe","eslint.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName has "\\node_modules\\" or ParentProcessName has "\\node_modules\\"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious Process Under node_modules Path
id: c4d6e8f0-1a2b-4c3d-9e5f-6a7b8c9d0e1f
description: Detects LOLBins or shells executing from inside a node_modules tree, or non-node binaries spawned by a node_modules executable — the blast surface of a compromised transitive npm dependency.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  in_node_modules:
    Image|contains: '\node_modules\'
  suspicious_lolbin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
  condition: in_node_modules or (ParentImage|contains: '\node_modules\' and suspicious_lolbin)
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\node_modules\\* OR *\\NODE_MODULES\\*) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node_modules\\* OR *\\NODE_MODULES\\*)) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*DownloadString* OR *Invoke-WebRequest* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *FromBase64String*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|bash|wscript|cscript|curl|wget|certutil|mshta|rundll32)\.exe$/i OR regex("(DownloadString|Invoke-WebRequest|IEX|FromBase64String|-EncodedCommand)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="*\\node_modules\\*" (Processes.parent_process_name NOT IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*powershell*","*cmd /c*","*-Command*","*curl *","*wget *")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="*\\node_modules\\*" (Processes.parent_process_name NOT IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*powershell*","*cmd /c*","*-Command*","*curl *","*wget *")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
npm pre/post-install Script Disabling Bypass Attempt AIInstallation High
Detects developers/CI re-enabling the lifecycle-script execution path that npm 12 disables by default — e.g. `npm install --ignore-scripts=false`, `--foreground-scripts`, NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false, .npmrc `ignore-scripts=false`, or `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` invoked outside an approval workflow. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact prose: GitHub is closing --ignore-scripts/lifecycle-hook execution by default, and the documented re-enable path is the `approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` workflow plus CLI flag/env overrides. .npmrc writes catch the persistent-config variant. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-install • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/
ATT&CKT1562 T1197
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Maintainer running `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` as part of GitHub-recommended upgrade workflow
  • Dev tooling installers (electron-builder, sharp postinstall) that legitimately require --foreground-scripts
  • CI runners reading NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS from a pipeline variable set by ops
  • Yarn migration scripts that touch .npmrc to set ignore-scripts=false during a controlled migration
  • Local dev sandbox environments where developers explicitly opt-in via env var
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending" and DeviceName in ("<known-maintainer-workstations>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm whether the host/user is going through the GitHub-recommended `npm approve-scripts` review (commit to package.json present) or is bypassing it interactively. Identify the package being installed when the bypass was set. 2) Contain — if unsanctioned, kill any in-flight install, revert .npmrc, unset env var, and quarantine node_modules. Force a clean `npm ci` with default settings. 3) Hunt — search the org for any other hosts/CI runners with the same env-var or .npmrc bypass, audit recent npm installs on those hosts for lifecycle-script execution (UC1 query), and check git history for unauthorised package.json `scripts` additions.
let CmdlineBypass = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--foreground-scripts","approve-scripts","--allow-scripts-pending","NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false","npm_config_ignore_scripts=false","--scripts=true");
let NpmrcEnables = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName == ".npmrc"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$";
union CmdlineBypass, NpmrcEnables
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=coalesce(AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName), FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let CmdlineBypass = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts=false","--foreground-scripts","approve-scripts","--allow-scripts-pending","NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false","npm_config_ignore_scripts=false","--scripts=true")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType="CmdlineBypass";
let NpmrcEnables = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType="NpmrcModified";
union CmdlineBypass, NpmrcEnables
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm Install-Script Bypass via CLI Flag or Environment
id: e2f3a4b5-6c7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b
description: Detects npm/node invocations that explicitly re-enable lifecycle scripts after npm 12 disables them by default — --ignore-scripts=false, --foreground-scripts, NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false, or approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending invoked interactively.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  npm_cli:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  bypass_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--ignore-scripts=false'
      - '--foreground-scripts'
      - 'approve-scripts'
      - '--allow-scripts-pending'
      - 'NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false'
      - 'npm_config_ignore_scripts=false'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:1 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPM.exe) @CommandLine:(*--ignore-scripts=false* OR *--foreground-scripts* OR *approve-scripts* OR *--allow-scripts-pending* OR *NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false* OR *npm_config_ignore_scripts=false* OR *--scripts=true*)) OR (@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.npmrc OR *\\.NPMRC)))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx)\.exe$/i regex("(--ignore-scripts=false|--foreground-scripts|approve-scripts|--allow-scripts-pending|NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false|npm_config_ignore_scripts=false|--scripts=true)", field=CommandLine)) OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\\.npmrc$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*--ignore-scripts=false*" OR Processes.process="*--foreground-scripts*" OR Processes.process="*--scripts-prepend-node-path*" OR Processes.process="*approve-scripts*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-scripts-pending*" OR Processes.process="*NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe") (Processes.process="*--ignore-scripts=false*" OR Processes.process="*--foreground-scripts*" OR Processes.process="*--scripts-prepend-node-path*" OR Processes.process="*approve-scripts*" OR Processes.process="*--allow-scripts-pending*" OR Processes.process="*NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
npm registry traffic to non-allowlisted registry host during install AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for outbound HTTPS connections during an active `npm install` to hosts that are not the standard npm/yarn/GitHub Packages registries — the article's --allow-remote default closure means any tarball/registry pull from elsewhere should now be exceptional. Correlates the network connection with a concurrent npm/node process on the same host. Rationale: Anchors on the article's --allow-remote default closure (remote tarball / non-default-registry pulls become opt-in). Filters known-good registries explicitly so the residue is unsanctioned-registry traffic during an npm process tree. Sentinel join uses ImNetworkSession (no ActingProcessName column) correlated to ImProcessCreate by host + 5-minute window. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/using-npm/registry
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal artifact-proxy registries (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio) hosted on company DNS
  • Yarn fetching from registry.yarnpkg.cn or other regional mirrors
  • Postinstall scripts of legit packages downloading prebuilt binaries from github.com release URLs (sharp, node-sass, esbuild)
  • node-gyp downloading the Node headers tarball from a custom NODE_GYP_FORCE_PYTHON mirror
  • Corporate proxy URLs configured in .npmrc strict-ssl=false for testing
Suppression filter
and not (RemoteUrl endswith "<your-internal-artifactory-domain>" or RemoteUrl endswith "objects.githubusercontent.com" or RemoteUrl endswith "github-releases.githubusercontent.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full DNS + connection chain for the host during the install window. Identify the unsanctioned host's owner (whois, threat-intel) and the package whose install triggered the pull. 2) Contain — block the destination at the proxy/firewall, isolate the host, and remove the package from node_modules. Rotate npm tokens stored on the host. 3) Hunt — search org-wide DNS logs for the same destination, query lockfiles for the offending package@version, and inspect any other hosts that hit the destination for follow-on payload execution.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm add","node-gyp")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where not (RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "npm.pkg.github.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "nodejs.org"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "objects.githubusercontent.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith "registry.npm.taobao.org")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let NpmInstall = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "npm.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "npx.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "yarn.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "pnpm.exe"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm add","node-gyp")
  | project NpmTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where isnotempty(DstHostname) or isnotempty(Url)
| extend DstHost = coalesce(DstHostname, tostring(parse_url(Url).Host))
| where isnotempty(DstHost)
| where not (DstHost endswith "registry.npmjs.org"
        or DstHost endswith "registry.yarnpkg.com"
        or DstHost endswith "npm.pkg.github.com"
        or DstHost endswith "nodejs.org"
        or DstHost endswith "objects.githubusercontent.com"
        or DstHost endswith "registry.npm.taobao.org")
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443)
| join kind=inner (NpmInstall) on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstHost, DstPortNumber, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\NPM.exe OR *\\NODE.exe) -@DestinationHostname:(*registry.npmjs.org OR *registry.yarnpkg.com OR *npm.pkg.github.com OR *nodejs.org OR *objects.githubusercontent.com OR *registry.npm.taobao.org)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| ContextImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=80
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i NOT regex("(registry\.npmjs\.org|registry\.yarnpkg\.com|npm\.pkg\.github\.com|nodejs\.org|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|registry\.npm\.taobao\.org)$", field=DomainName) | groupBy([aid, DomainName], function=count())}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") All_Traffic.dest_port IN (443,80) NOT (All_Traffic.dest="*registry.npmjs.org" OR All_Traffic.dest="*registry.yarnpkg.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*npm.pkg.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*registry.npm.taobao.org") by host All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") All_Traffic.dest_port IN (443,80) NOT (All_Traffic.dest="*registry.npmjs.org" OR All_Traffic.dest="*registry.yarnpkg.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*npm.pkg.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*registry.npm.taobao.org") by host All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry OS command-injection in HTTP requests to admin/MICS endpoints AIExploitation High
Hunts for shell metacharacters (;, |, backtick, $(), URL-encoded variants) in HTTP requests targeting Ivanti Sentry admin/MICS service paths — the documented OS command-injection sink in CVE-2026-10520. Article-specific: targets the public PoC pattern Shadowserver reports being weaponised at scale against Internet-exposed Sentry instances. Rationale: Article states the vulnerability is an OS command injection (T1190 → T1059) and that a public PoC is being weaponised against Internet-exposed Sentry admin portals. Sentry's historical attack surface is /mics/services/* on 8443 — pairing those paths with shell metacharacters yields very low FP outside scanner traffic.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, Nuclei) probing CVE-2026-10520 from approved source ranges
  • Penetration-test source IPs running the public PoC against own assets
  • Sentry self-monitoring health probes that happen to include encoded query strings
  • Legitimate admin URL with a literal pipe character in a config value (rare)
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("10.0.0.0/8", "<vuln-scanner-cidrs>") and RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "Nuclei", "Nmap")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the target host is an Ivanti Sentry appliance and pull the full RequestURL + response code; benign scanners almost always come from a known IP range and produce a 403/404 burst rather than 200. Step 2 — Contain: if the response is 200 and the source IP is not on the scanner allowlist, block the source at the perimeter, isolate the Sentry appliance from the internal estate, and snapshot for forensics. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the Sentry hostname for new outbound connections, shell spawn from gateway/Java services (UC2), and authorized_keys/cron modifications (UC3) in the 24h post-request window.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort in (443, 8443)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/mics/", "/sentry/", "MICS", "admin")
| where RequestURL has_any (";", "|", "`", "$(", "%3B", "%7C", "%60", "%24%28", "%26%26")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry gateway/Java service spawning interactive shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-10520 RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-10520: the Sentry web/Java service (tomcat/java/httpd/nginx) spawning bash/sh, curl, wget, nc, python or perl as a child process. Article-specific: maps to the 'execute code with root privileges' outcome and the backdoor-installation step Shadowserver observed on most exposed instances. Rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10520 yields 'code with root privileges' — the universal post-exploit tell on a Linux gateway is the web/Java service spawning a shell or curl/wget/nc to stage a backdoor (which Shadowserver confirmed has happened on 'most' exposed instances). Parent=service + child=shell/LOLBin is a near-zero-FP pair on an appliance.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor hotfix or patch installer scripts spawning bash/curl as part of the upgrade (correlate with maintenance windows)
  • Sentry health checks invoking curl to localhost endpoints
  • Legitimate admin SSH session that itself spawned an interactive shell (rule out via InitiatingProcessParent chain)
  • Container/orchestrator probes if the gateway is containerised
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("hotfix", "upgrade", "healthcheck", "localhost")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full process chain (Java → shell → next process) and the inbound HTTP request that immediately preceded the spawn (cross-ref UC1). Confirm DeviceName is genuinely a Sentry appliance, not a dev workstation named 'sentry'. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the appliance from internal networks (block egress at perimeter, leave management VLAN), preserve volatile memory and the /tmp/ working directory, rotate any credentials handled by the gateway (MDM enrolment tokens, backend service accounts). Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate new SSH authorized_keys entries (UC3), new cron/systemd units, outbound connections to non-corporate IPs in the last 30 days from this host, and pivot on the source IP from UC1 across the rest of the estate.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java", "tomcat", "httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "catalina.sh")
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
imProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("java", "tomcat", "httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "catalina")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Backdoor persistence on Ivanti Sentry: SSH authorized_keys modification or new cron/systemd unit AIInstallation High
Detects the persistence mechanisms Shadowserver observed on backdoored Sentry gateways: unauthorised SSH public-key additions to root or service accounts, new cron jobs, or new systemd unit files written post-exploitation. Article-specific: 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' — the persistence write is the strongest survival signal once initial access has succeeded. Rationale: Article explicitly reports the gateways were 'backdoored' — on Linux appliances the canonical persistence primitives are SSH authorized_keys, cron, and systemd. Writing to any of these on a hardened gateway by anything other than the vendor patcher is a high-fidelity backdoor signal.
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1053.003 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor patch (R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) installer rewriting systemd units
  • Authorised configuration-management (Ansible) push from a known control plane
  • Legitimate sysadmin rotating their own SSH key via change-controlled process
  • Internal SOAR playbook that drops a forensics-collection cron
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible", "puppet", "chef-client", "yum", "dnf", "rpm", "dpkg", "apt")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the file content (authorized_keys → diff against last known-good; cron/systemd → read the command it runs). If the entry runs an outbound connection, a base64 payload, or references /tmp/, treat as confirmed backdoor. Step 2 — Contain: remove the unauthorised key/cron/unit (capture content first), rotate root and all service-account credentials, terminate active SSH sessions originating from non-corporate IPs, and isolate the appliance. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on any IP in the dropped authorized_keys / cron command across estate-wide netflow, search for the same key fingerprint on other appliances, and check for matching CVE-2026-10520 exploitation hits in UC1 within ±24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has_any (@"/.ssh/", "/root/.ssh/") and FileName has "authorized_keys")
   or (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/var/spool/cron/"))
   or (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/", "/lib/systemd/system/") and FileName endswith ".service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
imFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/authorized_keys", "/root/.ssh/", "/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/lib/systemd/system/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry running version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for any Sentry instance whose installed version is older than the fixed releases (R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1). Article-specific: these are the exact patched versions Ivanti shipped Tuesday and Shadowserver warns anything older is 'most likely compromised'. Pairs with UC1/2/3 to scope blast radius. Rationale: Article names the exact fixed versions (R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) and Shadowserver's warning that unpatched = compromised — turning the version list into a TVM/asset query is a deterministic prerequisite for scoping. Internet-facing flag prioritises the immediately-exposed subset.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Air-gapped or lab Sentry instances that legitimately run older versions
  • Decommissioned-but-still-inventoried appliances
  • Defender TVM lag — version field not yet refreshed after a same-day patch
  • CMDB stale entry where the appliance has actually been retired
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: sort the result by IsInternetFacing=true and confirm each hit is a live, reachable Sentry. Cross-check with perimeter logs for hits on port 443/8443 from the public internet in the last 7 days. Step 2 — Contain: emergency-patch Internet-facing instances first (Ivanti R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 per branch); for any that cannot be patched immediately, drop the admin port at the edge until patched. Step 3 — Hunt: for every vulnerable Internet-facing host, run UC1 (exploitation), UC2 (post-exploit shell), and UC3 (persistence) over the window between the CVE-disclosure date and the patch-applied time, and treat any hits as confirmed compromise per Shadowserver guidance.

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Langflow CVE-2026-5027 exploit chain: /api/v1/auto_login token then POST /api/v2/files AIExploitation High
Detects the documented exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-5027 where an unauthenticated attacker first hits Langflow's auto-login endpoint to mint a session token, then within seconds POSTs to /api/v2/files to write an arbitrary file via the unsanitised filename multipart parameter. Correlating both URIs from the same source IP within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either endpoint individually. Rationale: Article explicitly names both URIs (POST /api/v2/files for the traversal, plus the unauthenticated auto-login step that mints the session token in 'a single unauthenticated request'). Pairing them in a same-source-IP / same-host time-window correlation eliminates the noise of either endpoint hit alone. Tenable TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC (github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027) both confirm the two-step pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/ • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the auto_login + file upload endpoints during authenticated scans
  • Langflow integration tests / CI pipelines that exercise the auto_login + file upload flow against a staging instance
  • Developer demo flows where a single user logs in and immediately uploads a flow JSON
  • Bug-bounty researchers / red-team engagements pre-notified to the SOC
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<scanner_ip_1>","<scanner_ip_2>") | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","InsightVM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr's geo and reputation, the User-Agent string, and the HTTP response code for the /api/v2/files POST (200 = file written, 403 = blocked). If response is 200, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: take the Langflow instance offline or front it with a WAF rule blocking POST /api/v2/files where filename contains '../'; rotate any secrets reachable from the Langflow host (API keys, OpenAI tokens, MCP creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host's DeviceFileEvents/FileWritten for files written by python/uvicorn outside the Langflow data dir (UC2), and check the host's process tree (UC3) for shells spawned from the langflow process. Confirm version is <1.9.0 (UC4) and upgrade to 1.10.0.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 120s;
let TokenHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v1/auto_login"
    | project TokenTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/files"
| project UploadTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| join kind=inner TokenHits on SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| where UploadTime between (TokenTime .. TokenTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', UploadTime, TokenTime)
| project TokenTime, UploadTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by UploadTime desc

Langflow Python process writes file outside data dir (CVE-2026-5027 post-exploit drop) AIInstallation High
Once the path-traversal write succeeds, the Langflow worker (python/uvicorn/gunicorn) is the process that writes the attacker-controlled file. Hunts for files written by that process to high-value system paths or with extensions/names indicating webshells, cron persistence, or SSH key implantation. Catches the post-exploit drop even when web/WAF logs aren't ingested. Rationale: Article confirms the impact is 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and VulnCheck honeypots observed 'test files' being dropped. The Langflow worker process is the only legitimate writer to its data directory, so a write by that process to /etc/, web roots, SSH key files, or cron from this process is the clean exploit indicator. Avoids false-positives on legitimate flow saves by anchoring on path/extension rather than just process identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1098.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow legitimately writing user-uploaded flow JSON or RAG corpus files to a non-standard data directory configured via LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR
  • Langflow component that writes logs to /var/log via a custom logging handler
  • Python pip install/upgrade of Langflow plugins writing into site-packages (often under /usr/local/lib/python*/)
  • Backup/sync tools running as the langflow service user touching shared paths
  • Custom-flow component using python-shell or os.system to legitimately write artefacts
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetFilePath has "site-packages" and TargetFileName endswith ".py") | where ActorUsername != "root" or TargetFilePath !startswith "/var/log/langflow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the dropped file and check VT/Defender verdict; examine the file content directly (cat the .php / .sh / authorized_keys) for webshell magic strings or attacker SSH keys. Cross-reference Timestamp with web-log POSTs to /api/v2/files (UC1) from external IPs within ±2 minutes. 2) Contain: quarantine the file, kill the Langflow worker process, rotate the service account, remove any added SSH keys / cron entries / WAR files, and block the source IP at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any child process spawned by the langflow worker (UC3); look for outbound connections from the langflow process to non-RFC1918 IPs in DeviceNetworkEvents in the prior 24h.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = pack_array(@"\langflow\", @"\.langflow\", @"\langflow_data\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow", "/tmp/langflow");
let SuspiciousPaths = pack_array("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\", @"\ProgramData\");
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","langflow_backend","-m langflow")
| where not(FolderPath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where FolderPath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = dynamic([@"\langflow\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow"]);
let SuspiciousPaths = dynamic(["/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow")
| where not(TargetFilePath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where TargetFilePath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Langflow worker spawns shell or LOLBin child (CVE-2026-5027 RCE) AIExploitation High
Path-traversal-to-RCE on Langflow typically ends with the python/uvicorn worker spawning a shell (bash/sh/cmd) or download utility (curl/wget) to fetch a second-stage payload after the implant lands. Detects any non-python child of the langflow worker process — Langflow legitimately runs sub-pythons only. Rationale: Tenable's TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC both demonstrate the path traversal escalating to RCE by writing an executable file the langflow worker later invokes — or by the upload handler triggering interpreter execution. Langflow's worker should only ever spawn other python interpreters (subprocess pools); a bash/curl/wget child of the langflow worker is a strong RCE indicator. Anchoring on parent cmdline containing 'langflow' avoids FPs from arbitrary python scripts on the box. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027 • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Langflow component that legitimately shells out (e.g. a flow node that runs a local CLI tool — git, ffmpeg, pandoc)
  • Langflow startup script using bash to source env vars or do tini-style init
  • Healthcheck probes that exec curl from the Langflow container to test connectivity
  • Developer using `langflow run` interactively in a terminal where the parent shell is recorded as parent of python
  • Backup component shelling out to tar/gzip from within a flow
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck" and ProcessCommandLine !has "--version" | where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","huggingface.co"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the ProcessCommandLine — look for base64 blobs, IPs/URLs being fetched, or output redirection to /tmp/.X paths. Pull the SHA256 of any downloaded file and check VT. 2) Contain: kill the Langflow process tree, snapshot the host, isolate via Defender or EDR isolation. Pull memory if a payload is likely in-memory only. 3) Hunt: identify all hosts running Langflow <1.9.0 (UC4) and check each for the same parent-child shape in the prior 14 days; pivot on outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the langflow worker for any non-pip/non-PyPI destinations.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o","socket.socket")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Langflow versions present in estate (CVE-2026-5027 exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Asset-hunting query to surface every host running Langflow <1.9.0 (or langflow-base <0.8.3) — the versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-5027 and the related Langflow CVEs (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017, CVE-2025-3248). Combines Defender TVM data with live process telemetry because pip-installed Langflow may not always be in the software inventory. Rationale: Article specifies the exact version boundaries: langflow-base <0.8.3 and Langflow <1.9.0 vulnerable; 1.10.0 is the latest. Cross-checked Tenable TRA-2026-26 and Snyk advisory. ~7,000 publicly-exposed instances per Censys means most orgs running it likely have unpatched copies — making asset discovery the first defensive priority. Combining TVM CveId lookup with live process telemetry covers both inventoried installs and shadow-IT pip installs that TVM may miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A test/staging Langflow instance intentionally pinned to an older version for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Langflow instance that doesn't reach the public internet (still worth patching but lower priority)
  • A Langflow fork or downstream redistribution that carries vendor backports of the fix without bumping the version string
  • DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities lag — recently-patched hosts may still show as vulnerable for up to 24h after KB sync
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the version observed by SSH'ing to a sample host and running `langflow --version` or `pip show langflow`. 2) Contain: for any exposed (internet-facing) instance, immediately gate behind a WAF or VPN, disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN by setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, and enforce LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER. 3) Hunt: for every vulnerable host in the list, run UC1 (web log chain), UC2 (file write), and UC3 (process spawn) against the last 30 days to confirm none have already been exploited; prioritise upgrade to 1.10.0.
let VulnerableLangflowCves = pack_array("CVE-2026-5027","CVE-2026-0770","CVE-2026-21445","CVE-2026-33017","CVE-2025-3248");
let TvmHits = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId in (VulnerableLangflowCves)
       or (SoftwareName has "langflow" and SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^(0\.|1\.[0-8]\.)")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source = "TVM";
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
    | summarize Timestamp = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | extend SoftwareName = "langflow (process-observed)", SoftwareVersion = "unknown", CveId = "CVE-2026-5027", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel = "High", SoftwareVendor = "langflow-ai", Source = "Process";
union TvmHits, ProcHits
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source
| order by Timestamp desc
